instructions: Set 3/4 cup of the butter and half the cream cheese (4 oz) on the counter to soften. They're for the filling and the frosting.
Rub 2 tsp of the butter around the inside of a 9 by 13 inch baking dish.

Stir the packet of yeast and 1 tsp of the granulated sugar into 1/4 cup warm water in a small bowl. The water should feel warm on your wrist, about 110°F. Leave it for 7 to 10 minutes, until it's foamy on top. If it doesn't foam, the yeast is too old, so start again with a fresh packet.

Meanwhile, put the 3/4 cup milk, 1/3 cup of the butter, the remaining 1/3 cup granulated sugar and 1/2 tsp of the salt in a small saucepan over medium low heat. Stir until the butter melts and the milk is warm.

You're warming the milk to 120 to 130°F, so if you have a thermometer, check it. No thermometer? It should feel hot on your finger, like a hot bath, with no steam coming off it. If it gets hotter than that, take it off the heat and let it cool for a few minutes before it goes near the yeast.
Put 2 cups of the flour in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the dough hook. Add the 2 eggs, the warm milk and the yeast mixture, and mix on medium low until it comes together.
Turn the mixer to medium and add 2 cups of the flour, 1/2 cup at a time. Stop adding as soon as the dough forms a soft ball that pulls away from the sides of the bowl. You may not need all of it.
Sprinkle a little of the remaining flour on the counter and transfer the dough onto it. Knead it for about 8 minutes, until it's smooth and springs back when you press it with a finger.
Put the dough in a large clean bowl and cover it with a kitchen towel. Leave it somewhere warm for about 1 hour, until it has doubled in size.
Meanwhile, stir the 1 cup brown sugar and 2 tbsp cinnamon together in a small bowl.
Dust the counter with the rest of the flour. Roll the dough out into a rectangle about 15 by 12 inches.
Spread 1/2 cup of the softened butter over the dough, right to the edges. Sprinkle the cinnamon sugar evenly over the butter.
Starting from one long side, roll the dough up tightly into a log. Cut it into 15 even slices with a sharp knife. This makes 15 rolls.
Set the rolls cut side up in the buttered dish. Cover them with the towel and leave them for 30 to 45 minutes, until they're puffy and touching each other. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 375°F.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the tops are golden brown and the rolls in the middle feel set when you press them.

While they bake, put the 1 1/2 cups powdered sugar, the 4 oz softened cream cheese, the last 1/4 cup softened butter, the 1/2 tsp vanilla and a pinch of salt in a bowl. Beat with a hand mixer or the stand mixer until fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Let the rolls cool in the dish for 10 to 15 minutes. Spread the frosting over them while they're still warm and serve.
method_notes: Both make an enriched yeast dough with warm milk, butter, sugar and egg, roll it into a rectangle, spread it with soft butter and cinnamon sugar, roll it up, cut it and give the rolls a second rise in a 9 by 13 inch dish. Spend with Pennies (the lead) proofs the yeast in water, warms the milk to 120 to 130°F, fills with brown sugar and tops the rolls with a cream cheese frosting. Natasha's Kitchen starts with a sponge of milk, yeast and a little flour, uses white sugar in the filling, cuts 16 rolls and pours a salted maple butter glaze over them. This follows the lead's dough, filling and frosting, which make 15 rolls.
